summary: Compare manual solutions list against existing task tree, find missing tasks

solutions.name: The 1% Treaty
solutions.summary: International treaty in which signatory governments redirect 1% of military spending (~$27.2B/yr) to pragmatic clinical trials, with an IAB-funded ratchet adding roughly 1%/yr; multiplies trial capacity 12.3x and cuts the disease-exploration timeline from ~443 to ~36 years.
solutions.audienceOrActor: National governments (sign/ratify); everyone else via the mechanisms below

solutions.name: Global referendum on the 1% Treaty
solutions.summary: A verified global vote (4.13B registered voters; 3.5% activism threshold, 51.6% coordination target) proving demand so politicians who refuse to ratify lose elections; the campaign's central YES action.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Individual voters worldwide; campaign org runs the platform

solutions.name: Vote-and-refer propagation (tell two people)
solutions.summary: Each verified voter recruits two more (sharing breakeven 1 in 8.66M, upside/downside ratio 8.7Mx); exponential referral is the core coordination engine of the referendum and Prize.
solutions.source: The Earth Optimization Prize, 'The Part Where You Tell Two People' — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/earth-optimization-prize.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Every individual voter

solutions.name: The Earth Optimization Prize (dominant assurance contract)
solutions.summary: Deposit money in a pool and recruit verified referendum voters to earn Earth Optimization Points (1 recruit = 1 point); if 2040 HALE + median-income targets are met, points holders split the pool; if not, depositors get ~9.03x their money back — zero-downside coordination funding.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Depositors/funders, individual recruiters, host institutions

solutions.name: Incentive Alignment Bonds (VICTORY bonds)
solutions.summary: Investors fund the ~$1B treaty campaign; once the treaty passes, 10% of redirected funds repays bondholders at ~272% annual returns and another 10% rewards treaty-supporting politicians (campaign support + post-office career prospects tied to a public voting scorecard), out-lobbying military-sector lobbying 13.7:1.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Institutional/family-office/retail investors; politicians as reward recipients

solutions.name: The $1B treaty lobbying campaign
solutions.summary: The 'Legal Bribery Machine': direct lobbying, super PACs, opposition research, celebrity endorsements, mass media, viral referendum budget, and legal drafting across US/EU/G20, financed by IABs; the financial plan is raise $1B, pass the treaty, manage $27.2B/yr (80% cures / 10% investors / 10% political incentives).
solutions.audienceOrActor: Campaign organization; IAB investors; lobbyists (including co-opted military-industry lobbyists)

solutions.name: dFDA (decentralized FDA / ubiquitous pragmatic trials)
solutions.summary: An open protocol that connects patients to trials of ranked treatments, records real-world outcomes automatically, and publishes comparative-effectiveness results — cutting per-patient trial cost from ~$41,000 to ~$929 (RECOVERY-style) and expanding global trial capacity 12.3x.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Builders/engineers, patients (1.08B willing participants), health systems, regulators

solutions.name: Decentralized Institutes of Health (DIH)
solutions.summary: The treasury coalition for the war on disease: receives treaty funds, allocates them via patient choice plus wishocratic voting, and pays for results instead of grant applications — a health-industrial complex with the coordination power of the military-industrial one.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Treaty signatories fund it; patients and voters allocate; researchers get paid for cures

solutions.name: Right to Trial & FDA Upgrade Act
solutions.summary: Model legislation creating an open-source FDA.gov v2 and a patient right to participate in pragmatic trials — the domestic legislative version of the dFDA.
solutions.source: Right to Trial & FDA Upgrade Act — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/right-to-trial-fda-upgrade-act.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Legislators; citizen-lobbyists pushing the bill

solutions.name: The Legislation Package (pre-drafted bills)
solutions.summary: Ready-to-hand model bills so supporters become 'the best lobbyist in history' — giving politicians finished legislation that helps people instead of waiting for them to draft it.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Citizen-lobbyists, legislators, campaign legal team

solutions.name: Direct philanthropic funding of pragmatic trials
solutions.summary: Even without the treaty, directly funding pragmatic trials costs ~$0.842/DALY — ~106x more cost-effective than bed nets — so donors can act unilaterally today.
solutions.source: The 1% Treaty impact paper, 'Direct Funding Still Excellent' — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/economics/1-pct-treaty-impact.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Philanthropists, foundations, health funders

solutions.name: The Loving Takeover (buy the military contractors)
solutions.summary: Buy activist-to-controlling stakes in every major military contractor (~$48.4B activist entry; ~$873B outright-control ceiling; ~$90–109 per human) and redirect their ~$1,425-per-dollar-ROI lobbying machinery toward the 1% Treaty — existing shareholders, employees, and directors get richer, hence 'loving'.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Investors, activist funds, universal owners, humanity collectively

solutions.name: Earth Optimization Services / Earth Optimization Fund (EOS equity)
solutions.summary: The Berkshire-style investment vehicle for the takeover: investors buy EOS equity, EOS buys the companies that already buy policy and points their lobbying at health and wealth; staged terminal values from $330M (Stage 1) to $452B (Stage 3), public listing once proof exists.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Investors (retail to institutional); EOS as operator

solutions.name: The Love Letter (one share + a letter to the board)
solutions.summary: The friendly front door of the Loving Takeover: buy one share of a lobbying company and send its board a letter that opens 'I love you' and shows redirecting lobbying makes them richer; ownership of one share legally compels an answer.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Any individual; one share makes the board answer

solutions.name: Shareholder derivative demand letter (the Funniest Lawsuit in the Universe)
solutions.summary: $200 buys one share (legally sufficient under DGCL § 327) to send a shareholder demand letter turning military-contractor boards into advocates for pragmatic trials, backed by quadrillion-dollar damages math; comes with a full toolkit — eight per-contractor fact sheets, board-member research guide, pro-bono/contingency counsel pitch, and a filing-day checklist.
solutions.source: The Funniest Lawsuit in the Universe — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/lawsuit.html (kit: pre-filled-demand-letters.html, board-member-research.html, counsel-outreach.html, filing-day-checklist.html)
solutions.audienceOrActor: Individual shareholder-plaintiffs plus recruited plaintiff-side counsel

solutions.name: Rule 14a-8 shareholder proposal
solutions.summary: The escalation step after the 60-day demand-letter window closes: SEC Rule 14a-8 proposal text, 500-word supporting statement, and corporate-secretary cover letter to force a shareholder vote on lobbying reallocation.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Shareholders meeting 14a-8 eligibility

solutions.name: The litigation phase (derivative complaint)
solutions.summary: If the board refuses: decision tree for board responses, a derivative complaint structural template, and a settlement-negotiation playbook for active litigation.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Plaintiffs and counsel

solutions.name: Demand-letter media blitz
solutions.summary: Simultaneous public distribution of the filing: press-release template with journalist target list, embargo sequencing, plus a plaintiff media kit (op-ed template, tweet thread, LinkedIn post, video script, interview Q&A, T+60d follow-up release).
solutions.source: The Press Release and Journalist List — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/press-release.html (kit: knowledge/appendix/plaintiff-media-kit.html)
solutions.audienceOrActor: Plaintiffs and campaign communications volunteers

solutions.name: The Court of Humanity
solutions.summary: A new court where any human can sue any government, sovereign immunity is not a defense, and the 1% Treaty is the standing settlement offer; build cost ~$30M, expected social value ~$11.4B.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Builders/funders create it; any human files as plaintiff

solutions.name: Humanity v. Government (plaintiff registration)
solutions.summary: The class action against the governments of Earth — three counts of negligent mass homicide with itemized damages (~billions of post-cutoff disease/aging plaintiffs) — with the treaty as the only workable remedy; individuals join by registering as plaintiffs.
solutions.source: Humanity v. Government — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/humanity-v-government.html (paper: 'The People of Earth v. Their Governments' via knowledge/papers.html)
solutions.audienceOrActor: Any human as plaintiff; legal volunteers

solutions.name: Notice of Termination to elected officials
solutions.summary: A performance review and termination letter addressed to every elected official with authority over military spending — citizens acting as the employers politicians work for.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Individual citizens/constituents

solutions.name: The Shirt (the Funniest Joke in the Universe)
solutions.summary: Write 'this t-shirt ended war and disease' on a shirt you own (raising its value by ~$10.6M of unrealized treaty value per wearer); a $50M seed program funds 1M wearers whose cascade gets billions wearing it on the same day so non-ratifying politicians lose elections; includes how-to-play rules, a card, and stranger-conversation scripts.
solutions.source: The Funniest Joke in the Universe — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/joke.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Any individual (marker + shirt); funders for the $50M seed program

solutions.name: The Vandalism Handout
solutions.summary: A printable one-sheet — side 1: how to vandalize a closet with the shirt message; side 2: what the shirt's recipient reads — for tucking into collars at scale.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Individual pranksters/distributors

solutions.name: Earth Optimization Day (August 6)
solutions.summary: One synchronized day a year when every human votes and wears the shirt; the treaty redirect percentage ratchets up another 1% and politicians who refused to sign become named entries on a public list.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Everyone; campaign org maintains the list

solutions.name: Correcting the AIs (RLHF seeding)
solutions.summary: When an LLM gives vague humanism about ending war and disease, thumbs-down the answer and paste the canonical Q&A (14 paste-ready entries) into the feedback field; enough independent corrections make the plan the models' default answer, compounding across releases — the shirt cascade applied to AI training data.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Any LLM user, across every model they use

solutions.name: Special Education / SE Bot
solutions.summary: EOS's free AI-tutored education that teaches each person the manual to the level their job needs, plus a social-media correction bot posting quantified rebuttals at ~$0.067 per belief change (~4.38M modeled belief changes/yr; universal-owner ROI 60.2:1 for a $1T AUM investor).
solutions.audienceOrActor: EOS/funders operate the bot; every human is the student

solutions.name: AI Coordination Army
solutions.summary: Personal AI agents doing the outreach, follow-up, and coordination humans evolved to be bad at — scaling one organizer's reach from hunting-party size (~20) to millions.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Any supporter with access to AI agents

solutions.name: The 20 Questions call script
solutions.summary: A call script for someone you love: ask them 20 questions that walk them to the conclusion, then get them to ask 2 more people — at an average of 2, it reaches 4 billion humans in 32 rounds.
solutions.source: The Most Important Secret in the World: 20 Questions to End War and Disease — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/questions.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Individuals calling friends and family

solutions.name: Presidential appointment cascade (Commission of the President)
solutions.summary: Every human is appointed President & CEO of Earth Optimization Services on camera (two questions, one commission, under two minutes) and inaugurates at least two successors — a binary tree reaching 8 billion in 33 generations; comes with a printable Commission, ceremony script, and 'Your Desk Is Ready, President' notification letter.
solutions.source: Earth Optimization Commission — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/earth-optimization-commission.html (artifacts: commission-of-the-president.html, presidential-inauguration-ceremony.html, president-notification-letter.html)
solutions.audienceOrActor: Every individual, as both appointee and appointer

solutions.name: The Funniest Show in the Universe
solutions.summary: An interview show where every guest is appointed President of EOS and asked how they'd optimize Earth using the two metrics (HALE, median income), each inaugurating two successors — the appointment cascade as media format.
solutions.source: The Funniest Show in the Universe — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/funniest-show-in-the-universe.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Hosts/producers; guests; podcasters adopting the format

solutions.name: Humanity Manager Employment Agreement
solutions.summary: A personal employment contract for 'the most important job on Earth, which is fixing Earth' — you already have the job; signing it is the commitment device.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Every individual

solutions.name: The educational film
solutions.summary: A 3-minute 1950s-educational-film-style orientation video, producible with AI for the budget of a medium wedding, as the mass-audience entry point.
solutions.source: How to End War and Disease (educational film) — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/educational-film.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Producers/creators make it; everyone shares it

solutions.name: Multi-format book distribution
solutions.summary: The manual repackaged for every channel — paperback, podcast/audiobook ('Skull Auditory Port Edition'), and a systematic checklist for platform-native repurposing across Medium, Substack, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Reddit, Hacker News, and short-form video.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Volunteers/creators repurposing content

solutions.name: The Decentralized To-Do List for Humanity
solutions.summary: A public accountability primitive: named individuals and institutions are assigned specific tasks (sign the treaty, embed the widget, fund the prize pool) with a live death-counter next to every unfulfilled task — anonymous inaction becomes named inaction priced in humans per day.
solutions.source: The Decentralized To-Do List for Humanity — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/humanity-todo-list.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Campaign platform assigns; named individuals/institutions complete

solutions.name: Nonprofit coalition activation
solutions.summary: Coordinate Earth's ~10 million nonprofits into the campaign via exact emails, a legal memo, and a four-stage activation funnel — organizations endorse, embed the referendum, and recruit their own members.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Nonprofit organizations and their leadership

solutions.name: Google Ad Grants voter acquisition
solutions.summary: A pre-built, ready-to-load Google Ads campaign template so nonprofit partners spend their existing $10k/month Google Ad Grants driving treaty referendum votes at near-zero marginal cost.
solutions.source: Pre-Built Google Ads Campaign for Coalition Partners — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/google-ads-campaign-template.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Nonprofit partners with Google Ad Grants

solutions.name: Voter Acquisition Grant (funding a coordinator)
solutions.summary: A grant-proposal template funding a coordinator that aggregates nonprofit ad grants, iframe voting-widget embeds, and communication channels into the largest public referendum on disease eradication ever run; tiers from $100K Year 1 to $50M by Year 5, with per-voter cost-effectiveness beating every existing global-health intervention.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Foundations/grantmakers fund; a coordinator org executes

solutions.name: Prize pilot hosting (Initiating Node)
solutions.summary: Recruit a qualified institution to host the first 90-day Earth Optimization Prize pilot — convene, publish, seed, and measure without becoming the mechanism's sovereign — using the sponsor-facing memo and reusable outreach email templates.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Universities and institutions as hosts; supporters send the outreach

solutions.name: Recruitment & Propaganda Plan (first 100,000)
solutions.summary: How to recruit 100,000 humans before you have a nonprofit, bank account, or anything to offer except the argument — 'a Kickstarter where the reward tier is possibly not dying'.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Early organizers and volunteers with zero resources

solutions.name: Getting Started (90-day campaign roadmap)
solutions.summary: A first-ninety-days operating plan for anyone running the treaty campaign with a nonprofit, a website carrying the voting widget, and the book — assuming no money, no staff, and four focused hours a day.
solutions.audienceOrActor: A single campaign operator

solutions.name: Open ecosystem and bounty model
solutions.summary: Get other people to build most of the dFDA through open APIs and bounties — 'like WordPress but for not dying' — instead of building it centrally.
solutions.source: How to Not Build Most of It — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/appendix/open-ecosystem-and-bounty-model.html
solutions.audienceOrActor: Third-party developers; bounty funders

solutions.name: API & data indexes for agents
solutions.summary: Machine-readable data indexes and APIs so developers and AI agents can build tools and integrations on top of the Disease Eradication Plan.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Developers and AI agents

solutions.name: Wishocracy (pairwise preference aggregation)
solutions.summary: Let billions of people say whether the next marginal public dollar buys another weapon system or another pragmatic trial — via random pairwise allocation (RAPPA), without lobbyists, committees, or middlemen; also the DIH's allocation governance.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Citizens allocate; governments/DIH adopt

solutions.name: Optimocracy: Optimal Policy & Budget Generators (OPG/OBG)
solutions.summary: Causal inference over cross-jurisdictional policy data from the ~10,000 places that already tried each policy, generating evidence-ranked policies and budgets that maximize median health and wealth.
solutions.source: Optimocracy: The Evidence Machine — https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/solution/optimocracy.html (specs: optimal-policy-generator-spec.html, optimal-budget-generator-spec.html, optimocracy-paper.html)
solutions.audienceOrActor: Governments, analysts, and EOS as the proof engine

solutions.name: Algorithmic public administration (replacement bureaus)
solutions.summary: Replace government intermediaries with deterministic functions: the Automated Revenue Service (74,000 pages of tax code to six lines of code), Universal Security Administration (80+ welfare programs to one for-loop), Decentralized Accountability Office (self-auditing ledger), and Decentralized Census Bureau (citizenCount() in 50ms).
solutions.audienceOrActor: Governments adopting; engineers building

solutions.name: The Aligned Election Commission
solutions.summary: Replace regulator-funded campaign finance with a single public alignment score for politicians, so electoral survival tracks alignment with citizens instead of donors.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Election reformers; governments

solutions.name: Department of Peace
solutions.summary: Wishonia's zero-lines-of-code replacement for the Department of Defense, premised on war being a negative-sum game the spreadsheet already rejects (first-principles optimal US military budget: $184B vs $886B actual).
solutions.audienceOrActor: Governments restructuring military budgets

solutions.name: Declaration of Optimization
solutions.summary: A signable document declaring that the purpose of government is to promote the general welfare, measured by median healthy life-years and median after-tax inflation-adjusted income — 'a polite request that they do so'.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Citizens and officials signing

solutions.name: The Planetary Constitutional Convention
solutions.summary: A standing deliberative process to stress-test and improve the Earth Optimization manual: revisions must cover ten governance functions, pass eleven constitutional constraints, and survive public adversarial review before ratification as the current manual.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Scholars, critics, and public participants

solutions.name: Fork the protocol (Earth Optimization Protocol v1)
solutions.summary: The whole plan is an open-source instruction manual for raising HALE and median income by 2040; anyone can fork it and improve it to help humanity win the Prize faster.
solutions.audienceOrActor: Anyone — contributors, rival implementers, other institutions

missing.proposedTask: Host a Funniest Show episode
missing.why: A podcaster/creator runs the appointment-cascade interview format with a guest. Turns existing shows into referral machines (priorities 2 and 6); natural child of the appointment-cascade task if that gets created.

missing.proposedTask: Sign your Humanity Manager Employment Agreement
missing.why: Sign the personal employment contract right after voting — a peak-commitment device (per the 'catch users at peak commitment' rule) that raises follow-through on referral and org-recruitment tasks.

missing.proposedTask: Fund the correction bot
missing.why: A funder (esp. universal owners — 60.2:1 ROI at $1T AUM) finances the social-media rebuttal bot at ~$0.067/belief change. Moves vote conversion (priority 1) at quantified cost; a builder sub-task ships the bot.

missing.proposedTask: Point your AI agents at the campaign queue
missing.why: A supporter connects their AI agent to the Optimitron MCP (getAIQueue already exists) so the agent does outreach and follow-up at scale. Multiplies one human's referral capacity from ~20 to millions (priority 2); the infrastructure is built, only the task is missing.

missing.proposedTask: Produce the 3-minute orientation film
missing.why: A creator makes the 1950s-style film with AI tools for wedding-budget money; everyone else shares it. Top-of-funnel discoverability (priority 6) feeding vote conversion; a share sub-task follows once it exists.

missing.proposedTask: Repurpose one manual chapter for one platform
missing.why: A volunteer picks a chapter and a channel (Substack, X thread, short-form video) from the distribution checklist and publishes. Priority-6 discoverability; naturally sharded into many claimable tasks (chapter × platform).

missing.proposedTask: Recruit your organization to endorse and embed the referendum
missing.why: A member sends their org's leadership the exact emails and legal memo from the manual; org endorses, embeds the voting widget, recruits members. Priority 3 at scale — the current single seeded org task doesn't scale without this generic version that mints per-org children.

missing.proposedTask: Load the pre-built Ads campaign into your nonprofit's Ad Grants account
missing.why: A nonprofit staffer imports the ready-made Google Ads template and spends their existing $10k/month grant on referendum votes. Near-zero-marginal-cost priority-1 vote acquisition; natural child of the org-activation task.

missing.proposedTask: Recruit a host institution for the 90-day Prize pilot
missing.why: A supporter sends the Initiating Node memo and outreach emails to a university/institution; the institution convenes, publishes, seeds, and measures the pilot. Unblocks the Prize's real-world launch — the current Prize task is funding-only.

missing.proposedTask: Recruit the first 100,000 with nothing but the argument
missing.why: Early organizers execute the zero-resource recruitment playbook. Caveat: this is an operator playbook more than a crowd task — may be better represented as the sum of the vote/refer/20-questions tasks above rather than its own task.

missing.proposedTask: Run the first ninety days
missing.why: A single campaign operator works the 90-day plan (nonprofit + widget site + book, 4 hrs/day). Like the item above, this is an operator doc; only create the task if the tree is meant to track the operator's own work.

missing.solution: Right to Trial & FDA Upgrade Act
missing.proposedTask: Ask your legislator to sponsor the Right to Trial Act
missing.why: A constituent sends their legislator the finished bill text. Domestic legislative path to the dFDA that works before the treaty; also a priority-5 leader touch.

missing.proposedTask: Hand your legislator a finished bill
missing.why: A citizen-lobbyist delivers a pre-drafted bill from the package to a specific legislator's office and logs the response. Priority-5 leader outreach with an artifact; the Right to Trial task above is the flagship instance.

missing.proposedTask: Charter the Decentralized Institutes of Health
missing.why: Builders and legal volunteers draft the treasury's charter and allocation governance (patient choice + wishocratic voting) so treaty funds have a destination on day one. Low campaign priority now, but the treaty's credibility depends on the receiving institution existing on paper.

missing.proposedTask: Fund or claim a dFDA bounty
missing.why: Funders post bounties on dFDA components; third-party developers claim and ship them. Converts the funding-only dFDA task into a doer pipeline — 'WordPress but for not dying'.

missing.proposedTask: Build a tool on the campaign APIs
missing.why: A developer or AI agent consumes the machine-readable indexes and ships an integration. Grows the builder ecosystem and priority-6 discoverability; pairs with the bounty task.

missing.proposedTask: Ship RAPPA allocation for the DIH
missing.why: Engineers build/ship the pairwise-allocation product a jurisdiction or the DIH can adopt. Proof-layer work per campaign policy — belongs under the root, not the campaign branch.

missing.proposedTask: Ship the Optimal Policy Generator
missing.why: Engineers/analysts build the cross-jurisdictional causal-inference engine and publish evidence-ranked policies. Proof layer establishing priority-6 trust in the quantified case.

missing.proposedTask: Build a replacement bureau
missing.why: Engineers implement one deterministic bureau (Automated Revenue Service, Universal Security Administration, etc.) as a working demo. Proof layer; low campaign priority.

missing.proposedTask: Publish the politician alignment score
missing.why: Builders ship a public per-politician alignment score. Adjacent to the IAB political-scorecard mechanism, so check for reuse before creating; proof layer otherwise.

missing.proposedTask: Publish the optimal military budget
missing.why: Analysts publish the first-principles $184B-vs-$886B analysis as a standing artifact. Evidence for treaty vote conversion but structurally proof-layer/post-treaty; lowest urgency in this list.

missing.proposedTask: Sign the Declaration of Optimization
missing.why: Anyone signs the document declaring government's purpose is measured by median healthy life-years and median income. A soft-commitment signable that can feed the vote funnel; check overlap with the referendum vote itself before shipping.

missing.proposedTask: Submit an adversarial review of the manual
missing.why: Scholars and critics file structured critiques against the ten functions and eleven constraints. Priority-6 trust: surviving public adversarial review is the credibility mechanism.

missing.solution: Fork the protocol (Earth Optimization Protocol v1)
missing.proposedTask: Fork the protocol and file an improvement
missing.why: A contributor or rival implementer forks the open-source plan and submits improvements. Keeps the plan honest and open; priority-6 trust signal.
